reading.body:
H5 Secaucus is a 38,000-square-foot data center in Secaucus, Hudson County, New Jersey, certified for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliance, with access to 10 carriers offering 100 Gbps connections. The operator publishes no total megawatt capacity for this facility. The building is designed to Tier III standards with 2N UPS power, multiple diesel generators providing 48 hours of runtime, and N+1 cooling redundancy.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 have published power capacity totaling 111.3 MW. H5 Secaucus is not among those five published figures, meaning its power budget remains unknown from operator disclosure. This absence of power specification limits any assessment of the facility's role in the state's AI infrastructure.

Without a published megawatt capacity, H5 Secaucus cannot be placed in the rank of AI-relevant scale. The 38,000 square feet of technical space could support significant compute density depending on power allocation and cooling delivery, but that potential remains unquantified by the operator. For readers tracking where power constraints may bind AI scaling, this facility contributes no measurement to the observable baseline.
